correctness.rationale: Under independent source-row sampling, p=k/s and the two distinct arc inclusion probability q=k(k-1)/(s(s-1)). Cov(R,T) is zero for disjoint source motifs and splits exhaustively into two-vertex overlaps n(n-1)(n-2) with contribution p²(q-p³), and one-vertex overlaps n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3) with p³(q-p²). Substituting q-p²=-p(1-p)/(s-1) gives -n(n-1)p³(1-p)² for s=n-1, or n(n-2)p³(1-p)(2p-1) for s=n. Independent algebraic checks at all k for n=3..15 and complete enumerations of row-regular digraphs for n=3,4 pass with exact rational covariance. These are finite corroborations; the overlap partition and double count prove all n.
residual_risks: The formula concerns NON-INDUCED triangles and independent fixed-size outgoing rows, not fixed in/out degree configuration models.

value.rationale: Reciprocity and cyclic feedback are natural graph motifs; their joint second-order statistic is a relevant null-model diagnostic. The exact half-target sign reversal caused solely by permitting self-loops demonstrates how otherwise apparently cosmetic row sampling conventions alter motif dependence; the complete all-n,k formula is independently useful.
residual_risks: This diagnostic is not a causal claim about empirical networks and does not generalize automatically to degree-constrained ensembles.

limitations: n>=3, source rows independent and have exactly k distinct targets, both orientations counted modulo cyclic rotation.
No induced-triad or fixed-indegree results; residual priority uncertainty for general row-regular motif enumeration.
